name: Ridiculous Gnome
description:
Shows your keyboard and mouse input on screen, in one of two modes.

Presentation: keys and shortcuts (Ctrl + Shift + T) at a fixed place on screen, as a subtitle, heading or corner card, and rings where you click. For screen recordings, tutorials and live demos.

Ridiculous: playful effects where you type and click.

What you type becomes visible on screen, also in screen shares and recordings. By default typed keys only show as classes (abc, 123, #!?) and shortcuts by name (Ctrl + T), never as the characters typed; this can be changed, or effects turned off, per app.

Effects for all apps need rg-helper, a small system service installed separately with root rights (see the GitHub page). Without it the extension runs in a limited mode: effects only for the shell itself, e.g. when typing in the Activities overview.
